conventions.convention: The quantum presentation is over F = Q(q), with q indeterminate and N ≥ 1. Its coproduct is Δ(E_i) = E_i ⊗ K_i + 1 ⊗ E_i and Δ(F_i) = F_i ⊗ 1 + K_i⁻¹ ⊗ F_i, where K_i = L_i L_{i+1}⁻¹.
The candidate antipode fixes coefficients, reverses multiplication, interchanges L_j and L_j⁻¹, and sends E_i to −E_i K_i⁻¹ and F_i to −K_i F_i.
A Hopf antipode satisfies both convolution inverse identities; compositional bijectivity is not required or asserted.

The ordered-basis operator multiplies equal pairs by q, flips increasing pairs, and sends a decreasing pair to its flip plus (q − q⁻¹) times the original pair. The normalized quadratic relation is (T − qI)(T + q⁻¹I) = 0.
Tensor products are algebraic, tensor sums are finite, tensor powers are left-associated, and V to the zeroth tensor power is the scalar field.
Generic mutual centralizers are equalities of matrix-algebra images over Q(q). Faithfulness of the abstract Hecke action is asserted for N ≥ n, rather than for all N and n.

load_bearing.statement: The candidate antipode descends to a well-defined F-linear anti-algebra map S: U_N → U_N satisfying m(S ⊗ id)Δ = uε = m(id ⊗ S)Δ. Thus U_N is a Hopf algebra; no bijectivity of S is asserted.

On the free associative F-algebra before quotienting, define an F-linear operation by fixing coefficients, reversing each word, and assigning L_j ↦ L_j⁻¹, L_j⁻¹ ↦ L_j, E_i ↦ −E_i K_i⁻¹, and F_i ↦ −K_i F_i.

alerts.finding: In Proof 2.1, lem-hh-quantum-and-hecke-tensor-actions-commute states: “every earlier summand restricts to $K_i\otimes K_i$ or $K_i^{-1}\otimes K_i^{-1}$, and every later summand to the identity.” This classification is incorrect for the displayed F_i coproduct sum. For a summand indexed by r and checked positions a,a+1, r < a gives the identity on those positions, whereas r > a+1 gives K_i⁻¹ ⊗ K_i⁻¹. For example, with n = 3 and a = 1, the r = 3 summand is K_i⁻¹ ⊗ K_i⁻¹ ⊗ F_i. The existing Cartan commutation check handles either location, so this is a local proof-text gap rather than a counterexample to the lemma.

seams_checked.note: The supplier defines a Hopf antipode by both convolution inverse identities without bijectivity. The assigned antipode lemma uses precisely that convention and proves its identities directly; it does not assume an antipode from the published bialgebra supplier.

The diagonal tensor action agrees with the supplier's bialgebra-module interface. The consumer uses explicit coproduct actions and makes no rigid-dual, inverse-antipode or automatic-braiding inference.

This is contextual prerequisite material. The consumer constructs its Hecke operator explicitly and verifies braid relations directly; it does not assert an algebraic universal R-matrix for the generic quantum algebra or invoke the all-module braiding theorem without its hypotheses.

The supplier distinguishes characteristic-zero generic semisimplicity from split formal deformation. The consumer instead proves its centralizers by classical commutants and regular matrix ranks, and asserts neither arbitrary-fiber splitness nor root-of-unity centralizer equalities.
